name: CROR Signals
statusNote: A content source superseded at parity by Clear Board — its aspect encodings feed Clear Board's Signals station — but kept live on its own page.
oneLiner: A focused signal-aspect trainer for Canadian railway conductors and engineers — every block and interlocking signal aspect rendered as a drawn SVG lamp stack, with Learn, Quiz, Build, Family-drill, and Exam modes.
stack: Vanilla JavaScript, ES modules, no framework or bundler
Node used only for a correctness linter; zero external library dependencies

components.name: Router + boot
components.desc: Hash router, service-worker registration, and an onboarding gate.

components.name: Signal renderer
components.desc: An audited SVG renderer, ported verbatim from the CN Conductor Trainer.

components.name: Content dataset
components.desc: The canonical audited aspect dataset plus 30 alternate hardware forms.

components.name: Quiz generator
components.desc: Ranks wrong answers by confusability, family, and lamp-stack distance so distractors are plausible.

components.name: Modes
components.desc: Quiz, Build (assemble a lamp stack from a name, checked by deep equality), Family drill, and a timed Exam with an 80% pass bar.

components.name: Progress + store
components.desc: Leitner spaced repetition (boxes 1-5) behind a single localStorage touchpoint.

components.name: tools/validate.mjs
components.desc: A correctness linter — duplicate ids, bad lamp codes, forbidden plate types, distractor counts.

dataFlow: A quiz question pulls a target aspect, renders a random hardware form, and ranks distractors.
The tapped answer is checked; the Leitner box and streak update and persist.
Feedback shows the rule reference and meaning, with an audio cue.
The last question rolls into a score plus a missed-list with retry.
Build mode runs the reverse path — assemble the lamp stack, checked by deep-equality diff.
integrations: Reuses two audited assets from the training-assistant / CN Conductor Trainer lineage: the SVG renderer and the encoded aspect dataset
30 alternate hardware forms cross-checked against 136 screenshots of a third-party incumbent app
Distribution path: static host, then a TWA wrap for Google Play
decisions: Correctness is the entire product moat — one rulebook edition is the sole authority, and unverified aspects are flagged, never guessed.
The validator hard-fails on any US-practice plate that doesn't exist in Canadian signalling.
Distractor quality is treated as a correctness requirement — the validator demands at least three plausible wrong answers.
Free plus an optional tip, no ads or in-app purchases — superseding an earlier paid plan.
A light, mobile-first skin — commercial products get a light skin.
Show nothing rather than something false, carried over explicitly.
